content:
Russia launched a large overnight attack on Ukraine in the early hours of Thursday, striking the capital Kyiv with ballistic missiles and hitting two foreign civilian ships carrying grain near the Black Sea port of Odesa, Ukrainian officials said. At least 10 people were injured across the country, and homes, shops, water supplies and heating networks were damaged in Kyiv and seven regions as winter closes in.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said ballistic missiles hit a shopping centre and two other buildings on the east bank of the Dnipro River, wounding seven people. Residents heard loud explosions late on Wednesday night, and warnings for people to remain in shelters stayed in place into the morning. According to Reuters, Russia's Defence Ministry said on Thursday that its forces had carried out a large overnight strike on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv.

The attack was not limited to the capital. Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said Russian forces had struck water supply facilities, heating networks, shopping centres and residential buildings in Kyiv and seven oblasts. In Kharkiv, a drone hit a high-rise residential building. In Dnipropetrovsk region, water utility facilities were attacked several times during the night, and in Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad shopping centres caught fire. In Zaporizhzhia, heating networks were targeted and a water pipeline at an industrial facility was damaged. By Thursday morning, consumers in seven Ukrainian oblasts were still without electricity, Koretskyi said.

Ukraine's air force said its defences had shot down and neutralised 87 Russian drones. In total, Russian forces attacked with ballistic missiles and 113 strike drones of various types from the evening of 25 November, according to Ukrainian military reports.

The most consequential part of the night's attacks may have happened at sea. Near Odesa, Russian forces attacked two foreign civilian vessels carrying more than 100,000 tonnes of grain, Koretskyi said. The ships were hit overnight as they sailed in the Black Sea, threatening not only their crews but also one of the world's most important food export routes. Ukraine is one of the largest exporters of wheat, corn and sunflower oil, and its grain shipments feed import-dependent countries across the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

Russia gave a different account of the incident at sea. Its Defence Ministry said its forces had struck a dry cargo vessel southeast of Odesa in the Black Sea overnight, alleging that the ship was carrying military equipment and dual-use goods to Ukraine, according to the Interfax news agency. Ukraine has not confirmed the identity or flag of either vessel, and the full extent of the damage has not been independently verified.

The grain-ship attacks drew a sharp reaction in Europe. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Moscow must take concrete steps to show it is willing to negotiate, and warned that attacks on merchant vessels threaten global food security. He urged Russia to demonstrate its readiness for peace talks with a ceasefire in the Black Sea, according to Yeni Safak. The appeal came as European leaders gathered in Brussels for a special summit on the European Union's next long-term budget and further financing for Ukraine.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday that Ukrainian intelligence believes Russia is preparing a new massed attack on energy infrastructure, logistics and the facilities that keep cities and communities functioning. He called for stronger air defences as the damage from the latest strikes was still being assessed. The warning underlines a pattern that has defined the war's recent phase: strikes aimed less at the front line than at the systems that keep Ukrainian cities warm, lit and supplied through winter.

The timing matters. With temperatures falling, damage to heating and water systems can leave entire apartment blocks without radiators and taps for days, and repairs are harder when repair crews themselves are working under air-raid alerts. Energy officials have spent months stockpiling equipment and building protective structures around power plants, but the scale of the overnight barrage, and the warning of a bigger one to come, shows how exposed the grid remains.

The exchange of fire ran in both directions. A Ukrainian drone attack killed at least five people and wounded three others in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia, a Russian-installed official said, as reported by Al Jazeera. Russian authorities also reported repelling drone attacks in the Tuymazinsky district of Bashkortostan and in the city of Nevinnomyssk in the Stavropol region. Ukrainian forces have increasingly targeted Russian oil infrastructure and logistics hubs deep inside Russian territory, and some military-focused reports put the scale of the overnight Ukrainian drone operation at several hundred aircraft, though that figure has not been independently confirmed.

The diplomatic backdrop is equally tense. Washington and NATO allies continue to pursue negotiations to end the war, while fighting intensifies and European support for Kyiv is debated in Brussels. Russia has recently revived its sweeping 2021 demands on European security, insisting on limits to NATO's presence in eastern Europe, a position that has hardened the divide between Moscow and Western capitals. Ukraine, for its part, has continued to strike Russian military targets, including its recent attack on the Savasleyka air base, which Kyiv said damaged five Russian jets.

For now, the immediate questions are practical: whether power, water and heating can be restored quickly in the seven affected regions, whether the grain vessels near Odesa can be repaired or their cargo salvaged, and whether Russia follows through on the larger attack Ukrainian intelligence expects as early as the coming nights. Each answer will shape how hard this winter is for millions of Ukrainians, and how much grain reaches world markets in the weeks ahead.

summary: Russian forces struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and attacked two foreign civilian vessels carrying more than 100,000 tonnes of grain near Odesa overnight, as Ukraine warned that intelligence points to an even larger assault on its energy infrastructure in the days ahead.
title: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles and strikes two grain ships near Odesa
